5300: apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine"):--sow.
5302: from ὕστερος; to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient):--come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse.
5303: from ὑστερέω; a deficit; specially, poverty:--that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want.
5304: from ὑστερέω; a falling short, i.e. (specially), penury:--want.
5305: neuter of ὕστερος as adverb; more lately, i.e. eventually:--afterward, (at the) last (of all).
5306: comparative from ὑπό (in the sense of behind); later:--latter.
5307: from to weave; woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted:--woven.
5308: from ὕψος; lofty (in place or character):--high(-er, -ly) (esteemed).
5309: from a compound of ὑψηλός and φρήν; to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant:--be highminded.
5310: superlative from the base of ὕψος; highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens:--most high, highest.
5311: from a derivative of ὑπέρ; elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity:--be exalted, height, (on) high.
5312: from ὕψος; to elevate (literally or figuratively):--exalt, lift up.
5313: from ὑψόω; an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively):-- height, high thing.
5315: a primary verb (used as an alternate of ἐσθίω in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively):--eat, meat.
5316: prolongation for the base of φῶς; to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative):-- appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think.
5317: of Hebrew origin (פֶּלֶג); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch:--Phalec.
5318: from φαίνω; shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally:--abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly).
5319: from φανερός; to render apparent (literally or figuratively):--appear, manifestly declare, (make) manifest (forth), shew (self).
5320: adverb from φανερός; plainly, i.e. clearly or publicly:--evidently, openly.
5321: from φανερόω; exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment:--manifestation.
5322: from φαίνω; a lightener, i.e. light; lantern:--lantern.
5323: of Hebrew origin (פְּנוּאֵל); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite:--Phanuel.
5324: from a derivative of φαίνω; to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle):--sight.
5325: from a derivative of φαντάζω; (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy"):--pomp.
5326: from φαντάζω; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre:--spirit.
5327: properly, strengthened from the base of πέραν or rather of ῥήγνυμι; a gap or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent):--valley.
5328: of foreign origin (פַּרְעֹה); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king:--Pharaoh.
5329: of Hebrew origin (פֶּרֶץ); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite:--Phares.
5330: of Hebrew origin (compare פָּרָשׁ); a separatist, i.e. exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary:--Pharisee.
5331: from φαρμακεύς; medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively):--sorcery, witchcraft.
5332: from (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician:--sorcerer.
5334: from φημί (not the same as "phase", which is from φαίνω); a saying, i.e. report:--tidings.
5335: prolongation from the same as φημί; to assert:--affirm, profess, say.
5336: from (to eat); a crib (for fodder):--manager, stall.
5337: apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked:--evil.
5338: probably akin to the base of φῶς (compare φθέγγομαι); brilliancy:--light.
5339: of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently:--forbear, spare.
5340: adverb from participle of φείδομαι; abstemiously, i.e. stingily:--sparingly.
5341: by transposition for a derivative probably of φαίνω (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout):-- cloke.
5342: a primary verb (for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, ; and ; to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows):--be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold.
5343: apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish:--escape, flee (away).
5344: of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman:--Felix.
5345: from φημί; a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame"):--fame.
5346: properly, the same as the base of φῶς and φαίνω; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say:--affirm, say. Compare λέγω.
5347: of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman:--Festus.
5348: apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at:--(already) attain, come, prevent.
5349: from φθείρω; decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable:--corruptible.
5350: probably akin to φέγγος and thus to φημί; to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim:--speak.
5351: probably strengthened from (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave):--corrupt (self), defile, destroy.
5352: from derivative of (to wane; akin to the base of φθείρω) and ὀπώρα (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves):--whose fruit withereth.
5353: from φθέγγομαι; utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental):--sound.
5354: from φθόνος; to be jealous of:--envy.
5355: probably akin to the base of φθείρω; ill-will (as detraction), i.e. jealousy (spite):--envy.
5356: from φθείρω; decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively):--corruption, destroy, perish.
5357: of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial"):--vial.
5358: from φίλος and ἀγαθός; fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue:--love of good men.
5359: from (the same as φιλάδελφος), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor:--Philadelphia.
5360: from φιλάδελφος; fraternal affection:--brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren.
5361: from φίλος and ἀδελφός; fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal:--love as brethren.
5362: from φίλος and ἀνήρ; fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife:--love their husbands.
5363: from the same as φιλανθρώπως; fondness of mankind, i.e. benevolence ("philanthropy"):--kindness, love towards man.
5364: adverb from a compound of φίλος and ἄνθρωπος; fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely:--courteously.
5366: from φίλος and ἄργυρος; fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious:--covetous.
5367: from φίλος and αὐτός; fond of self, i.e. selfish:--lover of own self.
5368: from φίλος; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while ἀγαπάω is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as θέλω and βούλομαι, or as θυμός and νοῦς respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness):--kiss, love.
5369: from φίλος and ἡδονή; fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous:--lover of pleasure.
5371: from φιλέω; friendly; Philemon, a Christian:--Philemon.
5372: from φιλέω; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity:--Philetus.
5374: from Φίλιπποι; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi:--Philippian.
5375: plural of Φίλιππος; Philippi, a place in Macedonia:--Philippi.
5376: from φίλος and ἵππος; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites:--Philip.
5377: from φίλος and θεός; fond of God, i.e. pious:--lover of God.
5378: from φίλος and λόγος; fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian:--Philologus.
5379: from φιλόνεικος; quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute:--strife.
5380: from φίλος and (a quarrel; probably akin to νῖκος); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious:--contentious.
5382: from φίλος and ξένος; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable:--given to (lover of, use) hospitality.
5383: from a compound of φίλος and πρῶτος; to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction:--love to have the preeminence.
5384: properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.):--friend.
5386: from φίλος and σοφός; fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher":--philosopher.
5387: from φίλος and (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian:--kindly affectioned.
5388: from φίλος and τέκνον; fond of one's children, i.e. maternal:--love their children.
5389: middle voice from a compound of φίλος and τιμή; to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something):--labour, strive, study.
5390: adverb from φιλόφρων; with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly:--courteously.
5391: from φίλος and φρήν; friendly of mind, i.e. kind:--courteous.
5393: active participle of the base of φλόξ; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian:--Phlegon.
5394: from φλόξ; to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion):--set on fire.
5395: from a primary (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze:--flame(-ing).
5396: from φλύαρος; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously:--prate against.
5397: from (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. prater:--tattler.
5398: from φόβος; frightful, i.e. (objectively) formidable:--fearful, terrible.
5399: from φόβος; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere:--be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly), reverence.
